captionClips.text: Begin with the closed unit interval and remove its open middle third.
Repeat the same removal inside every surviving interval.
After n stages, the surviving length is two thirds to the n.

properties.content:
remove the open middle third
— then repeat

captionClips.text: At stage n, there are 2 to the n minus one new gaps.
Finite length remains; only the limiting length vanishes.

properties.content:
Every finite stage still has positive length.
The limit is the delicate step.

captionClips.text: A surviving point has a ternary address made only from zeroes and twos.
Those endless left-right choices form an uncountable family.

properties.content: An address for every surviving point
Infinite binary choices cannot be listed one by one.

captionClips.text: The surviving lengths are one, two thirds, four ninths, eight twenty-sevenths.
Repeated multiplication by two thirds drives the sequence to zero.
The Cantor set has as many points as the full interval.
Yet its total length is zero.
